options.text: Sending the same prompt repeatedly until the answer improves
Breaking a big task into separate prompts, where each step's output becomes the next step's input
Writing one very long prompt with every instruction chained together
Linking several AI products in one browser window

questions.explanation: A chain is a relay race: focused legs, clean baton handoffs. Repeating one prompt (a) is rerolling, and one giant prompt (c) is exactly the juggling act chaining exists to avoid — the model does four jobs at once and each a bit worse.

questions.prompt: Why should a chain step's output be a strict shape (exact list or JSON, no preamble)?

options.text: Strict shapes make the model smarter
The output gets pasted into the next prompt verbatim — a friendly 'Sure! Here are the themes...' wrapper pollutes the next step's input
Humans find strict shapes easier to read

questions.explanation: The reader of a chain step's output isn't you — it's the next prompt. A clean baton (predictable shape, no chatter) hands off perfectly; wrapper text and commentary ride along into step 2 as noise. Strict lists work as well as JSON (c), and human readability (d) is beside the point mid-chain.

questions.prompt: Besides focus, what's the big practical advantage of running steps separately instead of one giant prompt?

options.text: You can inspect the output between steps and catch a mistake before it poisons everything downstream
Separate prompts are always cheaper in total
The model remembers each step forever

questions.explanation: Checking the baton between legs is the superpower: a wrong theme caught after step 1 costs one rerun; the same mistake inside a giant prompt silently corrupts the summary and you may never spot where. Chains can cost more total (b) and still err (d) — they just make errors visible and cheap to fix.

title: Design a chain
instructions: A neighborhood association collected 15 messy free-text survey responses about improving the local park, and wants a short summary for the next meeting. Design a chain and write its first step. Submit BOTH parts in one message: (1) a <plan> section listing 2–3 numbered steps, where each step names its one job AND the exact shape of its output (the baton it hands to the next step), and (2) a complete <step1> section containing the full, runnable first prompt: it must include 4–6 invented survey responses inside an XML tag, instruct the model to extract the shaped output your plan promised (e.g. a strict JSON list of themes with counts), and demand ONLY that output with no preamble or commentary.

rubric.description: The prompt contains a <plan> section with 2–3 numbered steps, each stating one job and its output shape.
The <step1> section is a complete runnable prompt including invented survey responses inside an XML tag.
Step 1's requested output is a strict machine-friendly shape (exact list or JSON with named fields) matching what the plan promised.
Step 1 demands ONLY the shaped output, with no preamble or commentary.
